issues.problem: The volume control and its effect are several screens apart. Item 3 (the total) comes first, then 11 exercise rows of 186-246 px each, then item 6 (what changes) and item 8 (Add). When an athlete taps + they see only the number change. Which exercise gained the set, the before → after, the minutes and the Add button are all 3 to 5 screens further down. The lede is also not 'two lines': it takes about 5 lines at 321 px of content width. The stepper's top value (36 on plan A, 60 on plan C) also goes past what fits the gym time (about 28 and 23 in the prototype). That is said only in the per-day headings, which sit 575 px or more below the control.
issues.evidence: measure.json, 390×844 planned: total control at 3,249 px, first day heading at 3,824, 'What changes' at 6,240, Add at 6,473. Total → preview is 2,992 px (3.9 screens) and total → Add is 3,225 px (4.2 screens). At 375×667: 3,010 px (5.0 screens) and 3,285 px (5.5 screens). The open section is 3,618 px tall at 390 and 3,699 px at 375. The rows add up to 2,256 px, and each row's controls wrap to 2 lines at 390 and 375, because the disclosure's content width is 321 and 307 px, below the draft's 343 px. The prototype's stepper lines read 'Stepper: 3–36 (fits the 60-min days: about 28)' (plan A) and '3–60 (fits the 45-min days: about 23)' (plan C) in architect-v2/stack-prototype-output.md. Screenshots: out/stack-total-390.png and out/stack-rows-375.png (about 2 rows per screen at 375).
issues.fix:
Reorder the open section so that the total, its effect and Add fit on one screen at 375×667:
1. A one-line lede.
2. The total control, with the sentence 'Fits your gym time up to about 28' beside its range.
3. Directly under it, the 'What changes' line (3 → 14 direct sets, muscles 1 → 16 of 19), one line per day ('Day 01 · Push: +4 · about 48 of 60 min'), and the Add button.
4. Then the stack by day as one-line rows (name · sets × reps · each arm). A tap on a row opens its reasons and its sets/Change/Leave out controls in place, one row open at a time.
5. Days, Forearm exercises a day and Holds go in a closed 'Settings' row that shows their current values in its summary.
Add a S4 acceptance check: at 375×667 and 390×844, the total control, the before → after line and Add are all on one screen when the total is scrolled into view.
Alternative: keep the section order and add a compact copy of the before → after line and the Add button under the total. The full list and preview stay below.

issues.problem: The number the athlete chooses appears nowhere else on the page, and it is in a different unit. issues.section: §3.2 'After Add' (Also add to Week 2) and §3.9; interaction with Plan
issues.problem: The chosen volume lives in one plan week, and the next week drops it without saying so. Plan generates Week 2 and Week 3 fresh from the split pool (up to recommendationLimit exercises a day). It does not copy Week 1, so a stack added to Week 1 is not in a week generated later, and nothing in Plan or on the page says so. For weeks that already exist, 'Also add to Week 2' is 'previewed in one line'. That writes up to 14 entries the athlete never saw, on days they never saw, into a week whose own entries differ. Separately, the preview does not show the day's exercise count. Plan's own builder puts 5 exercises in a 60-minute day, and the default stack makes it 9 (plan A: 5 → 9, 9, 8). The only hint is 'adds 4'.
issues.evidence: Home.tsx:1985-1999 (generateWeek builds the next week from getSplitExercisePool(...).slice(0, gymTimeBudget.recommendationLimit) with fresh prescriptions). gymTimeBudget.ts:21 (60 min: recommendationLimit 5). Draft line 285 ('previewed in one line, added with its own Undo'). architect-v2 output plan B: 11 exercises, 'Changes written: 14'. Plan A rows: 4, 4 and 3 added to 5-exercise days.
issues.fix:
1. Keep the athlete's total and settings per region in stackStore, not only per week.
2. When the trained or selected week has no stack and an earlier week does, the closed summary says 'Your stack is in Week 1, not Week 2 · Design for Week 2'. That control opens the full design for Week 2, with its rows, preview and Add, then Undo. Never a one-line preview.
3. Have Plan's 'Week N generated' toast say that the forearm stack was not carried over, with a link to the section. S3 owns Home.tsx.
4. Add each day's exercise count to the preview: 'Day 01 · Push: 5 → 9 exercises · about 48 of 60 min'.

issues.section: §4.3 item 6 (Change a planned exercise) and §1.8/§7.3 claim that the package's 'reduce, replace or defer' is met

issues.evidence: BoutListSheet.tsx (HEAD and main) has only 'Open this workout' (BoutItem.tsx:36, which needs a sessionId; planned bouts have none), 'About {name}' (:52) and 'How this is counted' (:58). grep finds no 'Open in Plan' or Swap in components/specialization outside PlanChangeSheet. Under the prompt, inside the tendon section, list the planned entries that load that area in the trained week, one row each. Each row gets inline actions:
- '−1 set'
- 'Move to another day': day chips in place

Build them on S3's applyPlanBatch and `remove`. For entries the stack wrote, also link to the stack's own row. Add these files to T3 and S3, and drop the 'without new plan controls' claim.

issues.section: §4.3 summary, §4.4 Lede and Method note, vs §4.4's own 'Never in the section' list
issues.problem: The tendon section's own copy uses words its render-test scan forbids, and that the owner's bar rules out ('no risk'). The summary 'not a risk score', the lede 'it is not a risk score' and the method note '…an injury predictor, which is why the page shows no ratio, threshold or risk' contain 'risk' three times, plus 'injury' and 'threshold'. The scan exempts only 'strain' in the lede. Either the test fails on the draft's text, or exceptions get added quietly. Putting 'risk' on a tendon screen, even negated, is exactly what the owner's bar excludes.
issues.evidence: Draft line 437 (summary), line 454 (lede), line 464 (method note) against line 465 ('risk, … injury, … threshold' are forbidden; only 'strain' is excepted). The package asks only to 'Explain that mapped exposure is incomplete and does not measure tissue strain' and to title it 'Tendon exposure' (START-HERE §6.2).
issues.fix:
Rewrite without the forbidden words:
- Summary: 'Sets by attachment area'.
- Lede: '…It counts sets. It does not measure what the tendon carries, and the exercise mappings do not cover everything you do.'
- Method note: 'Logged weight is not tendon force, and no study found ties a set count to how a tendon will respond, so the page shows no ratio or cut-off.'
Keep the scan list as it is. If the owner wants a negated phrase, list that exact sentence as an exception, as 'strain' is.

issues.problem: 'Leave out' is a button on one exercise row on one day, but it removes the whole movement, so rows on other days disappear too. The draft also never says what happens to the athlete's total. If the left-out sets are re-spread, other rows change silently, possibly off-screen. If the total drops, the number the athlete chose changes without them touching it. Either way it breaks 'the total is the athlete's choice' and 'nothing changes silently'.
issues.evidence: Draft line 280 ('Leave out (acts at once: the row becomes "Thumb abduction left out · Undo")'), line 344 ('the movement leaves this design at once'), and line 312 (only + and a changed total are specified). Plan B in the prototype writes one movement on two days ('Wrist Curl 3 + 2', architect-v2 output), so Leave out on the Day 01 row also removes a Day 03 row about 1,000 px away at 390.

Specify both effects:
1. The left-out movement's sets leave the design and the total drops by that many. Say so in the Undo line: 'Thumb abduction left out · total 14 → 13 · Undo'. Nothing is re-spread.
2. Label the button by what it does: 'Leave out wrist flexion (2 days)' when the movement has more than one row.
3. Add a stack.test.ts case: leaving out a movement changes no other row.

issues.section: §3.4 Needs step 3 (draft line 311), §0 item 3 (line 13), the lede (line 276), §3.13
issues.problem: The rule "evened out muscle by muscle" assumes every forearm muscle needs the same number of direct sets. No source supports that, and it is the opposite of the app's own reviewed content. Because the count is per muscle, the muscles that only one movement reaches always come out least served. Those are APL, EPL, EPB, FPL, ED, the supinator, PT and PQ, so their band and lever drills get the extra sets ahead of wrist flexion, wrist extension and deviation. Thumb isolation therefore grows with the total. That contradicts v1's reviewed rationale for 412 ("small-muscle coverage, not a high-volume default", mappings.ts:293), the package's §4.1 (thumb drills are "not automatically imported prescriptions") and its §5.1 checklist (no automatic 19-muscle escalation). The line "No movement or muscle is weighted above another" is false under this rule: weighting by muscle count favours the movements that reach only one muscle. The §3.13 numbers do not test this rule either. The architect-v2 prototype spreads "by exercise, never by muscle count" (architect-v2/stackDesigner.ts:429), so the 8/16/30 tables describe a different algorithm.
issues.fix: Spread sets beyond the floor by exercise, as the prototype does: each further set goes to the kept exercise with the fewest stack sets, then by need order. Do not count sets per muscle. Add a region-data flag (for example `coverageOnly`) on variants whose reviewed rationale says coverage, not volume (404 and 412–414). Such a variant stays at its floor unless the athlete raises its row or a target asks for it. Rewrite §3.1's need (3), the lede and the row reasons ("Evens out: …") to match. Re-run §3.13 with the rule as written and replace its tables. stack.test.ts should assert that thumb drills never exceed the floor without a row edit or a target.
issues.evidence: evening_sim.py, which models draft step 3 on plan A's movement and muscle structure from v1's reviewed direct rows. At a total of 30 the three thumb drills get 3 sets each (9 of the 27 added), wrist flexion and extension get 2, and radial and ulnar deviation get 1. At 40 the thumb drills get 4 each (12 sets) and wrist flexion gets 3. The prototype's own spread rule is at architect-v2/stackDesigner.ts:429-438.

issues.section: §3.3 the unit (line 290), §3.4 Coverage and Needs (lines 301, 308-311), §3.2 item 2 (line 277)
issues.problem: Holds count as direct sets and stand in for moving work. The unit "direct forearm sets" includes deliberate holds. Needs (2) and (3) read "direct sets" from the plan week as the calculator counts them, and nothing limits that to the Holds setting. So a plan's own farmer's walk or dead hang covers finger flexion, and with Holds Off the stack drops the Finger Curl. The package forbids exactly this. Its §3.2 says deliberate_isometric bouts must not be read as "repetitions or equal hypertrophy to dynamic sets". Its §2.2 says a carry's role is "a time-based stabilization record" that "does not convert the carry into wrist-curl sets". S14 is summarised as "No universal seconds-to-dynamic-set conversion". The word "direct" also changes meaning on one page. The page's muscle list sorts by direct bouts, meaning direct dynamic, so FDS with only hangs shows 0 direct on the page while the stack says it has direct work. Separately, under Max strength a seconds target is divided by the written 10 s (prototype stackDesigner.ts:288). A 120 s target becomes 12 hold sets, which is more than one exercise's cap of 3 a session and 2 sessions a week.
issues.fix: Keep two quantities. The athlete's total counts direct moving sets only. Holds are a separate line (hold sets and recorded seconds) and are never added into the total. Coverage and the per-movement need are read per mode: a hold never covers or serves a moving movement, and a moving set never serves a hold movement. A seconds target is filled at the growth hold length (30 s) whatever the goal, or the section says how many sets it would take and leaves the rest of the target short. Use words that match the page: "direct moving sets" and "holds". stack.test.ts should assert that a plan's own carry or hang never removes a moving movement from the design.
issues.evidence: holdcover.ts (architect-v2's designer, real catalog and calculator). Plan A with Holds Off adds Finger Curl, and muscles with direct work go 1 → 16. Plan A plus a Farmer's Walk (299) on Day 02, Holds Off: the plan's own direct sets read 6 (3 of them the carry), the start value is 16, and Finger Curl is absent from the stack. The prototype's coveredPairs() counts deliberate_isometric as covering (stackDesigner.ts:124, 201-208).

issues.section: §3.3 the unit and §3.4 "The count it promises" (lines 290, 331)
issues.problem: The unit is defined by category ("direct dynamic or deliberate-hold credit"), but coverage is defined by relationship = direct. These disagree on cat-300 Zercher Carry. That variant is a deliberate hold whose only forearm row is BR contributing isometric, and categoryFor(contributing, isometric, true) gives deliberate_isometric (rules.ts:60). A Zercher carry therefore counts as a "direct forearm set", and BR counts as a muscle with direct work, even though the hands do not grip and BR is a helper. Meanwhile coverage still treats elbow flexion as untrained. 02-design §8 calls this work contributing, not direct. The page also has no "planned direct count" today, only regionDistinctBouts (types.ts:891). The promise that the page's count equals the total therefore depends on a new derived number the draft never defines: how mixed bouts count, how bouts are deduplicated across muscles, and relationship versus category.
issues.fix: Define the stack's count in one shared, region-agnostic function used by both the page line and the stack. It counts distinct bout ids with a reviewed relationship = direct mapping on an own target, read as direct_dynamic, plus mixed bouts with such a part. Deliberate holds are counted as a separate number (see the holds finding). Contributing holds such as cat-300 BR are never "direct". Test it on cat-300, on a mixed bout, and on one set crediting three muscles that must count 1.
issues.evidence: zercher.ts. Plan A with the Hammer Curl removed and Zercher Carry (300) added: the plan's own direct sets read 3, muscles with direct work 0 → 1 (BR), the start value is 15 = 3 + 12, and the stack still adds Hammer Curl. Mappings: mappings.ts, the 300 rows (BR contributing isometric). Variant: variants/forearm.ts:155 (hold(), so deliberateHold true).

issues.section: §4.2 Change line and Weeks (line 431), §4.4 Change copy (line 457)
issues.problem: The baseline treats unknown as zero. The change line has no state for a last week that is not known. If the athlete finished no workout last week, the line compares 0 against the median and prints "Last week: 0 sets · median 16 · −16 sets". That is the package's "unknown as measured zero", which its own engine guards with state missing_current (reference_engine.py:144-146). A week is also "known" once any one workout is finished, so a week with one of four sessions logged becomes a baseline week. That lowers the median and can trigger "More than in any of the 4 weeks before" on a logging artefact. Package §6.2 says "Complete means training data completeness is known, not merely an absence of entries" and asks for "Not enough information" when tracking is incomplete. The copy also drops the scout's line that the logger does not mark warm-ups, so logged warm-ups are counted as work (tendon-copy.tsv). That is incomplete coverage the package asks to report (§6.2 step 9).
issues.fix: Add a state: when last week has no finished workout, show "No finished workout logged last week; nothing to compare" and no numbers. In the method note, say a week counts as known once one workout in it is finished, so a partly logged week can lower the baseline. Show each baseline week's count of finished workouts beside the median. Restore the line "Warm-ups are not marked in the logger, so any you logged are counted here as work." Cover all three cases in tendonAreas.test.ts.
issues.evidence: Draft line 431 lists the states Building, New, Both zero and comparison, with none for an unknown last week. reference_engine.py:144-146 has missing_current. START-HERE §6.2, the paragraph on "Complete". deviceWorkoutLog.ts:63-64: the logger never asks for warm-ups.

Rewrite specializationSeed.test.ts so that, after schema v1, seed v1, schema v2, seed v2 and seed v3, forearm_mappings_v1's 418 rows and their sources equal the fixture byte for byte, v1 stays published and mapping_version_problems is null for it. issues.problem: The copy credits the package's editorial defaults to studies.
